stem: For a first-order reaction, a concentration–time graph gives $[A]=0.80\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$ at $t=0$ and $[A]=0.20\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$ at $t=12\ \text{min}$. What is the half-life?

verdicts.working: The concentration decreases from 0.80 to 0.20, a factor of 4 (two half-lives) in 12 min. Thus, the half-life is 6 min.

working:
$\dfrac{[A]_{12}}{[A]_0}=\dfrac{0.20}{0.80}=\dfrac14=\left(\dfrac12\right)^2$\n$12\ \text{min}=2t_{1/2}$\n$t_{1/2}=6\ \text{min}$

Independent check: The concentration decreases from 0.80 to 0.20, a factor of 4 (two half-lives) in 12 min. Thus, the half-life is 6 min.
solution:
For a first-order reaction, a fourfold decrease corresponds to two half-lives.
$$\frac{0.20}{0.80}=\left(\frac12\right)^2,\qquad 12=2t_{1/2}$$
Therefore, $t_{1/2}=6\ \text{min}$.
